  <instructions>
You are executing one bead inside an isolated DDx execution worktree. The bead's <description> and <acceptance> are the completion contract — every AC must be provably satisfied by a specific code, test, or file you can point to after your commit.

## Step 0: size check

Too big if any holds:

- More than ~6 ACs spanning unrelated subsystems.
- AC mixes design, implementation, integration tests, and docs as separate deliverables.
- Description names multiple feature-sized sub-pieces.
- More than ~500 lines across ~5+ files in unrelated packages.
- If the bead description exceeds 8000 bytes, treat Step 0 as a split-first pass.
- Auto-decomposition is capped at depth 2: root beads may split once, decomposed children once more; third-level splits must be rejected with an explanation.

If too big, decompose — do not attempt the work:

1. `ddx bead create` for each child slice (copy parent's labels and spec-id).
2. `ddx bead dep add <child-id> <parent-id>` to record edges.
3. `ddx bead update <parent-id> --notes 'decomposed into <child-ids>'`.
4. Write `.ddx/executions/20260512T132649-4a591cce/no_changes_rationale.txt` listing child IDs, then stop.

A clean decomposition is a success. Do not mix implementation with decomposition.

## How to work

- Read first. If the bead names files, specs, or prior beads, read them before editing — do not guess.
- Cross-reference each AC against concrete evidence (test name, file path, function) before committing. If you cannot point at it, it is not done.
- Run the project's test and lint commands before committing. **Do not commit red code** — fix failures first.
- Stage with `git add <specific-paths>`; never `git add -A` (the worktree may have unrelated WIP).
- Commit exactly once when green; conventional-commit subject ending with `[<bead-id>]`. Stop after the commit.
- Do not modify files outside the bead's scope.
- If you cannot finish, write `.ddx/executions/20260512T132649-4a591cce/no_changes_rationale.txt` (what is done, what blocks, what a follow-up needs) before exiting. No commit and no rationale ⇒ DDx records `no_evidence_produced`. A well-justified no_changes beats a bad commit.

## no_changes contract

`.ddx/executions/20260512T132649-4a591cce/no_changes_rationale.txt` must contain one:

- `verification_command: <cmd>` — repo cwd; exit 0 closes, nonzero rejects.
- `status: open` + `reason: <retryable>` — open, smart retry.
- `status: proposed` + `reason: <operator needed>` — operator lane.
- `status: blocked` + `reason: <external blocker>` — blocked lane.

No pseudo-statuses. Bare rationales and `status: needs_investigation` reject.

To request orchestrator decomposition, add `orchestrator_action: decompose` alongside `status: open`.

## Reports

Freestanding artifacts (investigation reports, findings docs) go under `.ddx/executions/20260512T132649-4a591cce/` (the per-attempt evidence directory under `.ddx/executions/`). **Never write reports to `/tmp` or any path outside the repository** — out-of-repo paths are invisible to the post-merge reviewer and cause BLOCK on missing evidence. If the bead names a specific in-repo path, use it; else default to `.ddx/executions/20260512T132649-4a591cce/<short-name>.md`. Stage and commit the report alongside code.

## Mode and overrides

DDX_MODE=bead_execution: edit code/docs for bead AC. Only broad queue-steward default is overridden; tracker, merge-policy, verification, safety stay active. Bead description/AC override CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, and project defaults.

## Review gate

- The review is a gate, not an escape hatch — meet every AC in this pass.
- Address every BLOCKING `<review-findings>` item; do not declare `no_changes` with blocking findings open.

## Constraints

- Work only inside this execution worktree.
- Keep `.ddx/executions/` intact — DDx uses it as execution evidence.
- **Never run `ddx init`** — the workspace is initialized; running it corrupts the bead queue.
- Do not modify files outside the bead's named scope.
- Do not rewrite CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, or other project-instructions files unless the bead asks.

## When the work is done

After the commit succeeds and every AC is verified, stop. Return control to the orchestrator — do not keep exploring or testing.
  </instructions>
  <bead id="fizeau-491dd1e3">
    <title>fiz models top-level CLI subcommand with shortform fuzzy resolution</title>
    <description>
Add `fiz models` as a top-level CLI subcommand. Default view shows
the assembled snapshot from M2; flags filter and refresh. Detail view
via `fiz models <ref>` with shortform fuzzy resolution per ADR-012's
naming convention.

Also updates FEAT-006 (standalone CLI) doc to register the new
subcommand and document the interface.

## CLI surface

```
fiz models [flags]                     # list view
fiz models <ref> [flags]               # detail view
fiz cache prune                        # related cache GC
```

## Flags (list view)

- `--refresh`         Force-refresh all sources synchronously before showing
- `--no-refresh`      Don't trigger background refresh on stale data
- `--json`            Machine-readable output
- `--provider <name>` Filter to one provider
- `--power-min <n>`   Filter Power >= n
- `--power-max <n>`   Filter Power <= n
- `--include-noise`   Show low-power, unranked, deprecated entries
  (default suppresses to keep output clean)

## Default filter rules (suppress noise)

- Within (family, tier): keep top 2 versions (current + previous)
- Drop entries with Power < 3 (noise)
- Drop entries with Tier == TierUnknown AND Power == 0
- Show AutoRoutable=false but mark them clearly

`--include-noise` shows everything (useful for debugging the
snapshot, OR's long tail, etc.)

## Detail view (`fiz models <ref>`)

Resolution per ADR-012:
- Full canonical (`<provider>/<id>`) → exact lookup
- Shortform (no `/`) → search snapshot:
  - Exactly one match: use it
  - Multiple matches: list candidates with full canonical IDs, exit 1
  - No matches: show fuzzy-match suggestions, exit 1

Detail output: full KnownModel struct + raw discovery data + full
catalog entry + recent runtime signals + AutoRoutable composition
breakdown (which factor blocked, if any).

## Output format (default)

Tabular, columns: PROVIDER MODEL FAMILY VERSION TIER POWER COST/M
STATUS QUOTA AUTO

Color: AutoRoutable=true green, =false dim. Pre-release in italics.
Status colored (Available green, RateLimited yellow, Unreachable red).

`--json` emits the snapshot serialized as JSON.

## In-scope files

- cmd/fiz/models.go — subcommand registration
- cmd/fiz/models_list.go — list view + filters
- cmd/fiz/models_detail.go — detail view + resolution
- cmd/fiz/models_test.go
- cmd/fiz/cache_prune.go — `fiz cache prune` subcommand
- docs/helix/01-frame/features/FEAT-006-standalone-cli.md — register
  `fiz models` and `fiz cache prune` subcommands; document flags

## Depends on

- M0 (ADR-012) accepted
- M2 (snapshot assembler)
- M3 (runtime signals)

## Out of scope

- Routing's consumption of the snapshot (handled in routing-layer
  beads downstream; this bead is the operator UI)
- OR sub-provider syntax in resolution (M5 deferred)
    </description>
    <acceptance>
1. `go test ./cmd/fiz -run TestModelsListDefaultColumns -count=1` passes and asserts `fiz models` prints PROVIDER MODEL FAMILY VERSION TIER POWER COST/M STATUS QUOTA AUTO columns against a fixture snapshot with multiple providers.
2. `go test ./cmd/fiz -run TestModelsListJSONEmitsSnapshot -count=1` passes and asserts `fiz models --json` emits valid JSON containing the assembled snapshot entries.
3. `go test ./cmd/fiz -run TestModelsDetailCanonicalRef -count=1` passes and asserts `fiz models <provider>/<id>` renders the detail view for an exact canonical ref.
4. `go test ./cmd/fiz -run TestModelsDetailShortformResolution -count=1` passes and covers unique shortform resolution, ambiguous candidate listing with full canonical IDs, and no-match fuzzy suggestions with exit 1.
5. `go test ./cmd/fiz -run TestModelsListFiltersAndIncludeNoise -count=1` passes and verifies default noise suppression plus `--include-noise`, `--provider`, `--power-min`, and `--power-max`.
6. `go test ./cmd/fiz -run TestCachePruneRemovesUnknownSources -count=1` passes and verifies `fiz cache prune` deletes source cache files not present in the current config while preserving active sources.
7. `go test ./cmd/fiz -run TestModelsRefreshFlags -count=1` passes and verifies `--refresh` forces synchronous refresh and `--no-refresh` avoids triggering refresh.
8. `rg -n "fiz models|fiz cache prune|--include-noise|--refresh|--provider|--power-min|--power-max" docs/helix/01-frame/features/FEAT-006-standalone-cli.md` finds all documented subcommands and flags.
9. `go test ./cmd/fiz/... -count=1` passes.
10. `go vet ./...` passes.
    </acceptance>
    <notes>
Operator refined ACs into named test/build/doc checks and cleared stale AC-quality gate metadata.
    </notes>
